newsitem.title: USA: Zenith Q2 loss deepens after bad debt charge.
newsitem.headline: Zenith Q2 loss deepens after bad debt charge.

text.p: Zenith Electronics Corp reported a second-quarter 1997 net loss of $49.3 million or $0.74 a share which included a $15 million bad debt charge, large losses in its color picture tube operations and a $20 million decline in revenues.
In the 1996 second-quarter Zenith incurred a net loss of $33.2 million or $0.51 a share. Second-quarter 1997 sales fell to $262 million from $282 million in 1996.

"The difficulties experienced in the second quarter overshadow progress in many areas, including reductions of overhead expenses and programs to assure timely new product introductions," President Peter Willmott said in a news release.

More than half of the company's operating losses for the 1997 quarter resulted from the company's color picture tube plant in Melrose Park, Ill. Benefits from new automated processes there have not yet been realized, he said.

In addition, net results for the 1997 quarter include the $15 million charge related to bad debt for a South American customer's accounts receivable. As a result, Zenith said it has received a waiver of certain financial tests for the second quarter, related to its credit agreement.

Willmott said Zenith increased its domestic color TV market share in key large-screen categories during the quarter. However, in total, Zenith's Consumer Electronics revenues were down, reflecting lower video cassettee recorders (VCR) sales compared to the 1996 quarter.

Sales of Network Systems products -- analog set-top boxes and data modems sold primarily to cable television operators -- also were down in the quarter. Willmott said the company expects to begin shipments of digital set-top boxes to the Americast telecommunications venture in the third quarter.

For the first six months of 1997, excluding the bad debt charge, Zenith reported losses of about $60 million, compared with about $69 million for the same period of 1996. Including the charge, first half 1997 losses were $74.5 million, or $1.12 per share, compared with a first-half 1996 loss of $68.5 million, or $1.06 per share. First-half sales were $521 million in 1997 and $520 million in 1996.
Shares of Zenith closed up 5/16 to 12.
